stages.name: Vulnerable Operator Deployment
observables: IBM Turbonomic prometurbo agent version 8.6.0 through 8.17.6

stages.name: Excessive RBAC Provisioning
observables: Service account bound to ClusterRole with apiGroups: [""]
ClusterRole granting get, list, watch verbs on secrets resource
Implicit paths to cluster admin access via wildcards

stages.name: Unauthorized Secret Access
observables: Listing secrets in namespaces unrelated to the operator
Dumping database credentials or TLS certificates
API calls from unexpected IP addresses

scenario.summary: Attackers exploit Kubernetes operators that possess excessive RBAC privileges, often introduced through outdated or abandoned supply chain components in registries like OperatorHub. By compromising a controller or its service account, an attacker can leverage cluster-wide permissions to access secrets, including administrative tokens and API keys, leading to full cluster compromise.

meta.rationale: Start with production clusters running IBM Turbonomic or Datadog components. Focus on operators deployed via OLM/OperatorHub which are often outdated.
meta.hypothesis: A vulnerable or outdated Kubernetes operator is running with excessive ClusterRole permissions, allowing an attacker to exfiltrate cluster-wide secrets or establish unauthorized AI agent bridges to external endpoints.

hunt.name: Kubernetes Operator RBAC Abuse and Secret Theft
hunt.description: Kubernetes operators often rely on highly privileged service accounts to automate lifecycle management. This hunt identifies operators with known vulnerabilities, such as CVE-2026-6389 in IBM Turbonomic, and analyzes their prevalence and network behavior. By stack-counting operator versions and monitoring for outbound connections to non-internal IP addresses, we can identify misconfigured controllers or AI-enhanced operators acting as unauthorized gateways. The hunt moves from initial inventory scoping to behavioral analysis of network egress, identifying where excessive RBAC permissions may be serving as a silent backdoor.

config.content: SELECT device_uid, cve_uid, affected_package_name, affected_package_version, severity FROM hb_vulnerability_finding WHERE (cve_uid = 'CVE-2026-6389' OR instr(',' || '{{operator_packages}}' || ',', ',' || LOWER(affected_package_name) || ',') > 0) AND status != 'suppressed' AND collected_at >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days')
config.description: Identify assets running software versions impacted by CVE-2026-6389 or identified as potentially high-risk operators.
config.expected_signal: A list of asset IDs and vulnerable packages. Silence indicates no known operator vulnerabilities are reporting.

primitive_config.label: Scope vulnerable operator versions
primitive_config.content: SELECT device_uid, cve_uid, affected_package_name, affected_package_version, severity FROM hb_vulnerability_finding WHERE (cve_uid = 'CVE-2026-6389' OR instr(',' || '{{operator_packages}}' || ',', ',' || LOWER(affected_package_name) || ',') > 0) AND status != 'suppressed' AND collected_at >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days')
primitive_config.expected: A list of asset IDs and vulnerable packages. Silence indicates no known operator vulnerabilities are reporting.

config.content: SELECT package_name, package_version, device_hostname, COUNT(DISTINCT device_hostname) AS host_count, MIN(collected_at) AS first_seen FROM hb_software_inventory WHERE asset_scope = 'container_image' AND instr(',' || '{{operator_packages}}' || ',', ',' || LOWER(package_name) || ',') > 0 AND collected_at >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') GROUP BY package_name, package_version, device_hostname ORDER BY host_count ASC
config.description: Identify rare or outdated operator images across the fleet to highlight potentially unmanaged deployments and collect hostnames.
config.expected_signal: Rare operator versions stand out at the top of the count. The device_hostname values found here should be used to fill the scope_hosts parameter.

primitive_config.label: Stack-count operator images
primitive_config.content: SELECT package_name, package_version, device_hostname, COUNT(DISTINCT device_hostname) AS host_count, MIN(collected_at) AS first_seen FROM hb_software_inventory WHERE asset_scope = 'container_image' AND instr(',' || '{{operator_packages}}' || ',', ',' || LOWER(package_name) || ',') > 0 AND collected_at >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') GROUP BY package_name, package_version, device_hostname ORDER BY host_count ASC
primitive_config.expected: Rare operator versions stand out at the top of the count. The device_hostname values found here should be used to fill the scope_hosts parameter.

config.content: SELECT device_hostname, process_name, process_path, dst_endpoint_ip, dst_endpoint_port, direction, time FROM hb_network_connection WHERE (instr(',' || '{{operator_processes}}' || ',', ',' || LOWER(process_name) || ',') > 0) AND direction = 'outbound' AND dst_endpoint_ip NOT LIKE '10.%' AND dst_endpoint_ip NOT LIKE '172.16.%' AND dst_endpoint_ip NOT LIKE '192.168.%' AND ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0) AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days')
config.description: Identify operator processes communicating with external endpoints, which may indicate agent bridges or exfiltration.
config.expected_signal: Connections to the public internet from processes like 'prometurbo' or 'manager' restricted to scoped hosts. Standard controllers should primarily talk to internal API servers.

primitive_config.label: Operator network egress behavior
primitive_config.content: SELECT device_hostname, process_name, process_path, dst_endpoint_ip, dst_endpoint_port, direction, time FROM hb_network_connection WHERE (instr(',' || '{{operator_processes}}' || ',', ',' || LOWER(process_name) || ',') > 0) AND direction = 'outbound' AND dst_endpoint_ip NOT LIKE '10.%' AND dst_endpoint_ip NOT LIKE '172.16.%' AND dst_endpoint_ip NOT LIKE '192.168.%' AND ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0) AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days')
primitive_config.expected: Connections to the public internet from processes like 'prometurbo' or 'manager' restricted to scoped hosts. Standard controllers should primarily talk to internal API servers.

config.objective: Determine if any vulnerable or rare operator images are performing unauthorized network communication by specifically cross-referencing the versions identified in the scoping steps with the external destination IPs found in the network activity logs.

config.expected_signal: A verdict characterizing the risk level of each discovered operator.
config.success_criteria: A risk verdict citing specific hosts, operator versions, and destination IPs.

config.question: the agent-triage verdict identifies vulnerable versions (e.g. Prometurbo < 8.17.6) with unexplained external egress
config.condition: the agent-triage verdict identifies vulnerable versions (e.g. Prometurbo < 8.17.6) with unexplained external egress
config.description: Route findings for remediation if high risk is confirmed.
Analyze operator service accounts and apply PoLP.
config.instructions: For each flagged operator, extract its YAML manifest. Verify if the ServiceAccount is bound to a ClusterRole granting 'secrets' access. Update vulnerable operators like Prometurbo to the latest version and downscope RBAC permissions to the managing namespace only.

config.description: Record the findings and transition to monitoring.
config.instructions: Document the audited versions. Note any operators found in default registries like OperatorHub that have since been abandoned by the vendor. Feedback anomalous egress patterns to the detection team for permanent rules.
